data: Largest LEO broadband constellation — over 11,000 active satellites (as of October 2026)
SpaceX commercial constellation. Public deployment + status data from FCC filings + Jonathan McDowell's tracking + Starlink.com.

SpaceX's broadband LEO constellation — over 11,000 active satellites (as of October 2026) at 550 km altitude split across multiple shells (53°, 70°, 97.6° inclinations). First operational service 2019; achieved global coverage 2023. Each Gen-2 satellite carries laser inter-satellite links, allowing the constellation to route packets between satellites without ground station hops. Autonomous collision-avoidance system performed over 355,000 manoeuvres from June 2025 to May 2026.
Polar LEO comms — 66 operational sats +9 spares, GMDSS partner, global voice/data
First-gen LEO broadband — 648 sats in 12 polar planes
Amazon LEO broadband — 3,236 sats planned, commercial beta 2026
Only operational MEO commercial broadband — 20+ sats

Over 11,000 active satellites (as of October 2026) at 550 km in 53° / 70° / 97.6° shells — the largest LEO constellation ever flown. SpaceX broadband internet, operational since 2019. Autonomous collision avoidance + laser inter-satellite links. Visible as a train of bright dots crossing the sky in the days after each launch.
